title: Victor Marx: Colorado Governor's Race Under Scrutiny As Republican Candidate Faces Record Campaign Finance Fine, Exorcism Controversies And Showdown With Democrat Phil Weiser
excerpt: Colorado's race to succeed term-limited Democratic Governor Jared Polis has produced the state's most contentious gubernatorial contest in a generation, pitting Democratic Attorney General Phil Weiser, a former Supreme Court clerk who has filed 82 lawsuits against the Trump administration, against Republican Victor Marx, a first-time candidate.
content:
A Marine veteran who cannot say how many people he has killed, performs exorcisms over the phone and wants to “consecrate the state back to God” is the Republican nominee for governor of Colorado and he is running against one of the most qualified candidates in the state’s modern history.

With 14 days until Colorado voters choose a new governor on 3 November, the race to succeed term-limited Democratic Governor Jared Polis has produced one of the strangest and most scrutinised campaigns in the state’s recent history, defined by a record campaign finance fine, questions about violence, unverifiable war stories, and the theological ambitions of a Republican candidate who has never held public office.

Victor Marx, the Republican nominee for governor, performs exorcisms, over the phone, even. He faces allegations of campaign finance violations. A Daily Beast report highlighted Marx’s own accounts of committing physical violence against his wife and young son. And he cannot say how many people he has killed. His opponent is Democratic Attorney General Phil Weiser, a former law clerk to the late Supreme Court Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg who is considered the heavy favourite and whose campaign holds a fundraising advantage of roughly two to one heading into the final stretch.

Colorado Governor Race 2026: Who Are The Two Main Candidates For Colorado Governor?

Weiser has been the state’s top prosecutor since 2019. He previously served as the dean of the University of Colorado Law School, worked in the Obama administration, and clerked for Supreme Court Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg. He beat US Senator Michael Bennet in the Democratic primary in June. His running mate is Jefferson County Commissioner Lesley Dahlkemper.

Republican Victor Marx served as a Marine. He founded the Colorado Springs-based ministry “All Things Possible Ministries” and entered the race as a political unknown with a social media following of nearly 3 million. He defeated two sitting legislators — state Senator Barbara Kirkmeyer and Representative Scott Bottoms in the Republican primary. His running mate is retired Marine Colonel George Markert. 

Weiser, speaking after Marx won the Republican nomination, called his opponent “a threat to our state’s values and our future” who practises “a politics of deception, demonisation, and distraction.”

Colorado Governor’s Race: What Is The Record Campaign Finance Fine Against Marx?

With just a month before the November general election, Marx’s campaign was fined tens of thousands of dollars for hundreds of campaign finance violations. The fine, $57,647.16 for 210 violations, is believed to be the largest in Colorado history. 

The Colorado Secretary of State’s office said the campaign accepted 203 contributions well over legal limits to the tune of about $83,000. Marx’s campaign admitted to “unintentionally” accepting donations above the state’s legal limit and blamed the excess contributions on inexperience. Colorado’s constitution bars candidates for governor from accepting cumulative contributions from any one individual above $1,450.

The hearing officer noted aggravating circumstances: the volume and duration of the violations, their continuation after the state notified the campaign of the problems, the depositing of excessive cheques, and the campaign’s disregard of pop-up warnings on the state’s campaign finance website. The Marx campaign had tried to return some funds, but fell significantly short of the full required amount. The Marx campaign did not respond to requests for comment on the fine.

Colorado Governor’s Race: What Are Exorcism Controversies Surrounding Marx?

As part of his ministry, Marx has said that he routinely encountered and exorcised demons from people, including from individuals he claimed were possessed due to the influence of pornography or being an unmarried couple living together. These exorcisms were sometimes performed over the phone.

An investigation by 9News of Marx’s activities in the last 15 years indicated that his work casting off demons is at the centre of his $7.5 million per year ministry, and can fairly be described as his life’s work. Marx told Colorado’s 9News: “What I’m doing is just praying for people who have been oppressed by evil, and the results are astonishing.” 

Marx has called on supporters to participate in a 21-day fast based on Biblical principles, with his wife Eileen declaring in a video message: “This is not just an election, but this is a spiritual battle against the forces of wickedness.” Marx himself, speaking at a campaign event, said: “I’m going to consecrate the state back to God.” 

When asked about his exorcism work, Marx told Denver7 at a campaign event in Windsor at the weekend that the negative coverage amounted to propaganda. “All the allegations and they’ve all been proven false,” he told Denver7’s Tyler Melito. “I think it’s pretty sad when politicians are so desperate they build these false narratives and allegations and lies. People are just tired of it.”

Colorado Governor’s Race: Has Marx Faced Questions About Violence And Unverified Claims?

Recordings show Marx describing violent incidents involving his wife and his toddler son in 2021. He described what he called a “bouncing push” against a door, recounting it with a laugh in one recording. He also told a Turning Point USA Pastors Summit: “I feel like God gave me a gift for violence, against a manifestation of evil.”

Marx has declared that he shoved his wife in the past and told donors he would do it again. His wife, Eileen, appeared alongside him during a donor call, placing her arms around his neck. Marx said he initially shared the account as a warning for young fathers, urging people to get psychiatric help, and said: “I did not hurt my son.”

Marx mentioned in an interview with 9News anchor Kyle Clark that he is unsure how many people he has killed and said he thought the exact details did not need to be clarified. When asked whether he had killed more people, he responded: “Does it matter?” 

Marx’s campaign website removed a claim that All Things Possible had rescued 45,000 women and children from abuse, after it was disproved.

Colorado Governor’s Race: How Have Republicans Responded To Marx’s Candidacy?

The reaction within Marx’s own party has been deeply divided. Former Republican Congressman Ken Buck crossed party lines to endorse Democrat Phil Weiser for governor. “I’m supporting Phil because I think he has the experience and he has the character to be a good governor,” Buck told Colorado Politics in an interview. He added: “If he won, how would he put a government together?”

Buck’s endorsement was one of more than a dozen from current and former Republican members, including former legislators, state officials, county commissioners and municipal leaders. 

Neither of Marx’s primary opponents, Kirkmeyer nor Bottoms, endorsed him after his June primary victory. Congresswoman Lauren Boebert was among those who appeared alongside Marx at a campaign event in Windsor at the weekend, telling Denver7: “I have learned that the Democrats cannot stand Victor Marx, and it makes me love him so much more.”

Marx, for his part, has embraced his position as an outsider. “The people are the one who’s going to put me in office, not the establishment, not the critics,” he told Denver7’s Melito at the Windsor event. “Whether it’s a Republican, unaffiliated or Democrat, the pain point here in Colorado is so high for the lack of affordability. It is not safe, and people are ready for politicians in leadership positions to be held accountable.”

Colorado Governor’s Race: Where Does The Race Stand Heading Into Its Final Weeks?

Weiser is considered the race’s heavy favourite, having raised at least $8 million in campaign funds compared to Marx’s $4 million. Marx has struggled to sustain the fundraising pace that helped him narrowly win a three-way Republican primary. Colorado has elected only one Republican governor in the past 56 years, Bill Owens, who won in 1998. Democrats hold a clear voter registration advantage across the state.

Rob Preuhs, political science chair at Metropolitan State University of Denver, told Denver7 that the final two weeks of the race were vital for Marx if he was to pull in any undecided unaffiliated voters but estimated that only around 5% of the electorate remained genuinely persuadable. “By this time, we’re talking maybe 5% generously that haven’t decided who they’re going to vote for,” Preuhs said.

Colorado political analysts have noted that Marx supports MAGA policies aligned with those of US President Donald Trump, and that mainstream and establishment Republicans have refused to support him. Weiser, they note, has had the good fortune of a badly divided Republican Party that nominated a controversial and politically weak political newcomer for governor.

Election Day in Colorado is 3 November 2026. Mail ballots have already been issued to voters across the state.
